newsitem.title: USA: BellSouth changes Wireless Cable buy terms. [CORRECTED 15:30 GMT]
newsitem.headline: BellSouth changes Wireless Cable buy terms. [CORRECTED 15:30 GMT]

text.p: BellSouth Corp on Wednesday said it finalized its earlier agreement to buy Wireless Cable of Atlanta and its licenses for wireless cable television in the city for stock valued at $46.9 million.
The agreement crystallizes a deal first announced on October 24. However the terms have changed (corrects from changed considerably.)
BellSouth will now exchange 0.49 of its shares for every Wireless Cable share, instead of the 0.5 (corrects from 0.9) originally offered, a BellSouth spokesman said.

Wireless Cable of Atlanta shares reached a year high of $19-3/4 soon after the news was announced today, before settling at 19-1/2, up $2, by 0945 EST/1445 GMT. It was trading at $13 in October before the deal was first announced.
BellSouth stock was at $45, down 1/8, which means the offer for the Wireless Cable of Atlanta is worth just over $22 per share at current prices.
"This acquisition is good news for potential video customers in Atlanta," said William Reddersen, BellSouth Group President of Long Distance and Video Services.
Wireless cable beams television signals by line of sight to receiver boxes mounted on the side of homes.
After accounting for the value of the existing 9,000 analog subscribers, the purchase price represents a cost of approximately $39 per potential line-of-sight household served, BellSouth said.
Assuming no delays in building the digital facilities, BellSouth could begin providing digital cable TV service to households in the Atlanta area in late 1997.
The purchase is subject to approval by industry regulators and Wireless shareholders. ((-- New York Newsrom 212 859 1610))
